title: Design a REST API
description: Understand REST API design principles and best practices.

options.text: REST APIs should use verbs in URL paths (e.g., /getUsers, /deletePost)
options.explanation: REST uses nouns for resources (/users, /posts) and HTTP methods (GET, DELETE) for actions. Verbs in URLs is an anti-pattern.

options.text: Idempotency means calling an operation multiple times produces the same result as calling it once
options.explanation: GET, PUT, and DELETE should be idempotent. POST is typically not idempotent. Idempotency is crucial for retry safety in distributed systems.

options.text: HTTP 200 is the correct status code for a successful resource creation
options.explanation: 201 Created is the correct status for successful resource creation. 200 OK is for successful retrieval or update operations.

options.text: GraphQL is a type of REST API
options.explanation: GraphQL is a distinct query language and runtime — it uses a single endpoint with POST requests, while REST uses multiple endpoints with HTTP methods.
